item.title: Bind Mounts Across Mount Namespaces: Four PRs and a Container Escape
item.description: GitHub Actions has a container: key that runs a job’s steps inside an image of your choosing. It’s popular because it gives you a reproducible toolchain without building a custom runner image. On a self-hosted runner it works by having the runner drive Docker. On ephemerd, “Docker” is a shim that speaks the Docker API and creates containers in containerd. Getting bind mounts right through that shim took four PRs in a week. A couple of months later the version that worked turned out to be an escape.

item.title: Zero-Dependency Deployments - Single Binary for WordPress
item.description:
The standard way to run a WordPress site is four services:

  • nginx for HTTP and TLS
  • php-fpm to run PHP
  • MySQL for data
  • Redis, once the site gets slow enough that someone installs an object cache plugin

That’s four processes and four config files. There are three sockets between them and four things to upgrade. For a big site that’s fine. For a brochure site or a staging copy it’s absurd. The same goes for a PR preview, a box at the edge, or a CI job that needs a real WordPress to test a plugin against.
